besu.name: Besu
besu.summary: Start with failed-frame reporting, precompile output and inclusion, and range-filter consistency. Individual replay also needs a scope decision.

erigon.name: Erigon
erigon.summary: The tested development build agrees on several cases that differ in the release, including tree lookup, MCOPY and historical system state. Default filter composition still needs attention; signed-transaction validity checks and error codes need alignment with the proposal.

nethermind.name: Nethermind
nethermind.summary: Prioritize complete error responses, retained execution output, and empty trace selections. Tree lookup and stack-word encoding also need API agreement.

reth.name: Reth
reth.summary: The main changes are tree-path lookup, filter composition, replay metadata, and missing code changes in state/VM traces. Signed execution validation matches the proposed requirements; error codes still need alignment.

build_notes.text: **The nightly is newer despite its lower version number.** Its commit is from September 20, while the release commit is from September 17. The release-only version bump set `2.6.0`; the nightly still declares `2.5.2`. [Compare the tested revisions](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/compare/73a3a00862a8f14f89e30da8de001456f18cfae0...03cb186c1d36eebbacc7bda08f36e25711d0804e).

geth.name: Geth draft fork
geth.summary: The experimental fork implements an earlier draft; unknown call fields and the proposed unknown-block code need updates. It is not upstream Geth support. Filtering remains a bounded scan and pruning coverage is incomplete. Signed execution validation matches the proposed requirements; error codes still need alignment.

besu.observed: Individual transaction replay is unavailable.
besu.change: Add `trace_replayTransaction`, or agree that it is outside the supported profile.

besu.observed: A recipient-only filter returns 1 of the 2 expected calls. Every recognized `mode` value is rejected with `-32602`, including `intersection` and `union`.
besu.change: Make a one-sided query select every call matching the populated list. Accept `intersection` as the default and `union` as an explicit option; reject only unknown values.

erigon.observed: Both lists are combined with OR by default (6 records instead of 1). With `mode: "intersection"`, a one-sided filter returns `[]` instead of treating the empty side as unrestricted. The unrecognized `mode: "garbage"` is accepted and treated as union.
erigon.change: Make intersection the default. Under either mode, ignore an omitted, null or empty side. Reject unknown mode values with `-32602`.

reth.observed: Both lists are combined with OR by default (6 records instead of 1). One-sided and explicit-mode queries agree.
reth.change: Take up Alloy #4216, which makes intersection the default and keeps explicit union, then retest.

nethermind.observed: `mode: "union"` returns the intersection (1 record instead of 6). The unrecognized `mode: "garbage"` is accepted.
nethermind.change: Implement `union` as matching either populated list. Reject unknown mode values with `-32602`.

besu.observed: An empty sender list with a populated recipient list loses expected matches.
besu.change: Treat `[]` like an omitted list, then apply the populated list normally.

nethermind.change: Treat `[]` as unrestricted, just like an omitted address list.

reth.observed: Null address lists are rejected, while the revised draft treats them as unrestricted.
reth.change: Accept null like an omitted or empty list, then apply the other filter normally.

besu.observed: PoS blocks include a synthetic PoW reward record.
besu.change: Remove the placeholder reward. This also changes which records pagination counts.

nethermind.observed: PoS blocks include a synthetic PoW reward record.
nethermind.change: Remove the placeholder reward and exclude it from pagination.

besu.observed: Unknown transactions can return [] and an unknown selected block returns null.
besu.change: Return `null` for an unknown transaction, so callers can distinguish absence from a transaction with no call records.

erigon.observed: Missing-transaction lookup can return an RPC error, and an unknown filter endpoint can return [].
erigon.change: Return `null` for a missing transaction or path; reserve errors for unavailable history and invalid requests.

nethermind.observed: Missing transactions or paths can produce exceptions/RPC errors.
nethermind.change: Return `null` for an absent transaction or path, while preserving distinct unavailable-history errors.

reth.observed: Missing individual replays return an error; verified pruned-history requests use `-32603`.
reth.change: Return `null` for absent transactions. For known transactions whose state is unavailable, use the proposed history-unavailable error (`4444`) rather than an internal error.

geth.observed: Unknown selected blocks use a different error code from the revised draft.
geth.change: Use -32001 for unknown blocks, preserving null for missing transactions and 4444 for pruned state.

besu.observed: Failed frames lose result information; a failed root precompile can also lack an error.
besu.change: Keep the error on the failing frame. Preserve revert bytes and measured gas when available; otherwise use an explicit `null` result.

nethermind.change: Keep an explicit result: preserve revert output and measured gas where available, otherwise return `null`.

besu.observed: A successful creation reports deployed bytecode under `output`.
besu.change: Use `code` for deployed bytecode, alongside `address` and `gasUsed`.

besu.observed: The zero-fee call with an empty trace selection is rejected.
besu.change: Recheck after the unsigned-call fee change (H15). This case alone does not establish a separate empty-selection bug.

erigon.observed: Empty-selection requests include rejected calls; the zero-fee case also fails the fee rule.
erigon.change: Accept an empty selection and return the execution envelope. Recheck alongside H15 before treating every rejection as a separate selection bug.

nethermind.observed: An empty trace selection triggers an internal reduction error.
nethermind.change: Execute the call and return its output with the unrequested components empty/null.

besu.observed: Marker probes execute wrong-chain and ordinary-code-sender transactions. Nonce, funds, intrinsic-gas and base-fee failures instead return empty success-shaped traces; these do not prove execution.
besu.change: Apply selected-state execution validity before running signed transactions. Distinguish validation rejection from execution failure, and use the proposed -32003 code for validation errors.

erigon.observed: Marker probes execute nonce mismatches, both insufficient-funds cases and ordinary-code-sender transactions. CREATE uses the state-nonce address. Chain, intrinsic-gas and base-fee failures are rejected with -32000. Review feedback supports stricter validation.
erigon.change: Apply selected-state execution validity before running signed transactions. Distinguish validation rejection from execution failure, and use the proposed -32003 code for validation errors.

nethermind.observed: Marker probes execute nonce mismatches and ordinary-code-sender transactions; CREATE uses the state-nonce address. Other invalid probes produce malformed JSON, which does not establish skipped validation.
nethermind.change: Apply selected-state execution validity before running signed transactions. Distinguish validation rejection from execution failure, and use the proposed -32003 code for validation errors.

reth.observed: All invalid probes in the validation corpus are rejected, using -32000 or -32003. Valid EOA/delegated controls execute, and valid execution-OOG returns a trace halt.
reth.change: Retain execution validation and align rejection codes with the proposed -32003 mapping once agreed.

geth.observed: The draft fork rejects nonce mismatches, but rejection codes need alignment with the proposed -32003 mapping.
geth.change: Apply selected-state execution validity before running signed transactions. Distinguish validation rejection from execution failure, and use the proposed -32003 code for validation errors.

besu.observed: Zero-fee unsigned simulations fail; callMany can wrap that failure inside result.
besu.change: Allow zero-fee `trace_call` simulations while retaining the selected block’s `BASEFEE` opcode value.

erigon.observed: Explicit zero-fee unsigned calls are rejected.
erigon.change: Allow zero-fee unsigned simulation without changing the block’s `BASEFEE` opcode value.

nethermind.observed: The empty-selection call fails; the other checked zero-fee calls do not.
nethermind.change: Resolve the empty-selection error (H11). These results do not establish a general zero-fee admission bug.

besu.observed: The `MCOPY` step omits its memory write.
besu.change: Include the bytes written at offset 32 in that step’s memory delta.

erigon.observed: The `MCOPY` step omits its memory write.
erigon.change: Record the same-step memory delta, including the copied word at offset 32.

besu.observed: The identity precompile returns bytes in the execution envelope but not its call frame.
besu.change: Copy the precompile’s return bytes into the call-frame result as well.

besu.observed: CREATE and SELFDESTRUCT address queries disagree with the corresponding block trace.
besu.change: Match creation by creator/created address, and SELFDESTRUCT by destroyed account/beneficiary.

besu.observed: A handled child failure can mark a successful parent or sibling as failed.
besu.change: Track errors per frame; a caught failure must not change the outcome of another frame.

besu.observed: A range filter differs from concatenating the same blocks’ traces across a fork boundary.
besu.change: Use each block’s own execution rules and make range filtering agree with per-block tracing.

besu.observed: Nested precompile frames are omitted even when their value is nonzero.
besu.change: Retain nested precompile frames with transferred or inherited nonzero value. Continue omitting zero-value nested frames and retaining root frames.

erigon.observed: Root and nested `trace_get` requests fail or select the wrong record.
erigon.change: Interpret the selector as one `traceAddress` path: `[]` selects the root, `[0]` its first child.

nethermind.observed: `trace_get` returns a list and treats positions differently from a nested path; `[]` returns `[]`.
nethermind.change: Return one object for one `traceAddress` path. `[]` selects the root; a missing path returns `null`. This changes the response type.

reth.observed: The selector uses a flat index; `[]` returns `null` and nested paths do not work.
reth.change: Walk one `traceAddress` path instead. Return the root for `[]`, and one object or `null` for other paths. Existing flat-index callers will need a migration path.

erigon.change: Return `trace: []` when call traces were not requested; keep the execution output independently.

nethermind.observed: Selecting only `stateDiff` loses nonempty execution output.
nethermind.change: Always retain output bytes. The return-42 fixture should still return its 32-byte word when only state differences are requested.

erigon.observed: Malformed raw transactions and an unknown option use error codes other than `-32602`.
erigon.change: Use JSON-RPC invalid params (`-32602`) for malformed input, separately from execution rejection.

nethermind.observed: Malformed raw input, negative filter count and integer paths expose validation differences across the captured builds.
nethermind.change: Return invalid params (`-32602`) for malformed encoding.

besu.observed: Wrong address-list types and negative count can return results rather than invalid params.
besu.change: Validate filter types and bounds and return -32602 for invalid request shapes.

reth.observed: An integer trace_get path returns null instead of invalid params.
reth.change: Reject integer path entries with -32602; callers must convert output path integers to hex quantities.

geth.observed: Unknown call-object fields are rejected by the older draft implementation.
geth.change: Ignore unknown call fields for forward compatibility while validating known fields.

erigon.observed: A historical beacon-root lookup includes a following block’s system update.
erigon.change: Read the selected block’s post-state, before applying the next block’s system operations.

nethermind.observed: VM stack words use padded byte strings.
nethermind.change: Serialize stack words as minimal hex quantities, e.g. `0x2a` rather than a 32-byte padded string.

nethermind.observed: Rejected signed transactions can leave truncated JSON on the wire.
nethermind.change: Finish validation before committing a streamed result, or ensure the error path returns one complete JSON-RPC response.

besu.observed: The initial zero-fee callMany result contains a complete JSON-RPC error envelope nested inside result.
besu.change: Return a top-level error when execution is rejected; never serialize an error envelope as a successful result.

nethermind.observed: Pre-Cancun account deletion does not report the expected code/nonce deletion markers.
nethermind.change: Report the removed code and nonce with deletion markers before Cancun; retain existing accounts under EIP-6780.

reth.observed: Pre-Cancun account deletion loses code/nonce deletion markers.
reth.change: Report the removed code and nonce before Cancun; preserve existing accounts after EIP-6780.
Include the requested transaction hash in the replay envelope, consistently with block replay.

reth.observed: EIP-7702 delegation code changes are missing from `stateDiff`.
reth.change: Include net authorization code set, replacement and clearing, even for existing accounts and when the subsequent execution reverts.

reth.observed: Creation `vmTrace.code` does not contain the expected executing initcode.
reth.change: Attach the creation frame’s initcode to its VM trace, including in block replay.

besu.observed: Omitting fromBlock starts at head 48. Supplying only toBlock 2 fails because the implicit start is later than the end.
besu.change: Start at the genesis (earliest) block when fromBlock is omitted; keep the supplied toBlock.

nethermind.observed: Omitting fromBlock starts at head 48. A toBlock-only query errors with from 48 greater than to 2.
nethermind.change: Use the genesis (earliest) start for an omitted fromBlock and preserve the requested end.

besu.observed: trace_callMany with one argument returns -32602 Invalid number of params; explicit latest returns NUMBER 48.
besu.change: Accept an omitted block argument and execute against latest.

reth.observed: An omitted trace_callMany block returns NUMBER 49, while explicit latest and trace_call defaults return 48.
reth.change: Default trace_callMany to latest; retain pending only when explicitly requested and supported.

besu.observed: trace_filter with safe or pending bounds returns -32603 Internal error; earliest succeeds. Pending call simulations return NUMBER 48.
besu.change: Resolve safe/finalized tags when available. Define or explicitly reject pending per method, without an internal error.

reth.observed: trace_filter rejects earliest, safe and pending with -32602, although numeric bounds work. Explicit pending call simulations return NUMBER 49.
reth.change: Accept resolvable mined-block tags for filter bounds. Decide pending filter support separately from its simulation behavior.
